name: Intravascular Large B-Cell Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on histopathology and clinical presentation

criteria.description: Presence of large neoplastic B-cells confined within the lumina of small blood vessels
Immunohistochemical positivity for B-cell markers (CD20, CD79a) in intravascular tumor cells
Multisystemic symptoms including neurological deficits and skin lesions without lymphadenopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma with supportive immunophenotyping and compatible clinical presentation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires biopsy of affected tissue demonstrating characteristic intravascular infiltration

pathognomonic.symptomName: Intravascular proliferation of large atypical B-cells

pathognomonic.notes: Erythematous plaques or nodules due to vascular occlusion
searchTerms: skin lesions from blood vessel lymphoma

common.notes: Including cognitive impairment, hemiparesis, or cranial neuropathies

searchTerms: losing weight and sweating at night

common.symptomName: Dyspnea due to pulmonary vascular involvement
searchTerms: shortness of breath from lung vessels
breathing difficulty due to lung blood vessels

occasional.notes: Less common than in other lymphomas

occasional.symptomName: Renal impairment due to vascular occlusion
searchTerms: renal impairment due to vessel blockage

occasional.notes: Due to vascular occlusion and thrombosis

imaging: MRI showing multifocal ischemic lesions in brain
CT scan may show pulmonary infiltrates without lymphadenopathy
PET-CT may show increased uptake in affected organs
other: Histopathology demonstrating large B-cells confined to small vessel lumina
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD20, CD79a, BCL-2

distinguishingFeatures: Mass lesion in CNS rather than intravascular localization
Presence of parenchymal tumor mass on imaging
Tumor cells infiltrate dermis and subcutis, not confined to vessels
Presence of nodules or tumors rather than vascular occlusion
Laboratory evidence of hemolysis and thrombocytopenia

redFlags: Rapidly progressive neurological deficits without clear cause
Unexplained persistent fever with systemic symptoms
Cutaneous lesions with vascular occlusion and no lymphadenopathy
references: Ponzoni M, Ferreri AJM, Campo E. Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma: a neoplasm of 'homeless' lymphocytes? Hematol Oncol. 2018;36(1):3-10.

Ferreri AJM, Campo E, Seymour JF, et al. Intravascular lymphoma: clinical presentation, natural history, management and prognostic factors in a series of 38 cases, with special emphasis on the 'cutaneous variant'. Br J Haematol. 2004;127(2):173-183.
